newsitem.title: USA: Ampace sees MDX unit hurting revenue goal.
newsitem.headline: Ampace sees MDX unit hurting revenue goal.

text.p: Ampace Corp said Thursday that reengineering costs at its MDX unit will hurt the company's chances of achieving its revenue goal of $40 million in 1997, although it is optimistic about the unit's longer term prospects.

In a statement accompanying second quarter earnings, released today, Bruce Jones, chairman and chief financial officer said: "The good news to report regarding MDX is that we began a reengineering program there in the second quarter. We are optimistic that a turn around of MDX will be completed by the third or early fourth quarter and it will improve our overall profitability. But the MDX reengineering adversely affects our goal to reach $40 million in revenues by the end of 1997, as originally planned."
The trucking company reported no per-share earnings (profits of $3,540) in the second quarter, versus a loss of $0.08 in the year-earlier period.
